3 The Armand Bayou is a slow-flowing river that forms an aquatic ecosystem in Texas,
North America.
Some biologists decided to study two invasive alien species of aquatic plants that are commonly
found in the Armand Bayou: water hyacinth, Eichhornia crassipes, and malancha, Alternanthera
philoxeroides. Water hyacinth and malancha reduce biodiversity in the Armand Bayou.
Water hyacinth is a floating plant that grows on the surface of the river. Water currents and the
wind can move water hyacinth plants from one place to another.
Malancha has roots that attach the plant to the soil at the edge of the river. Malancha grows
and reproduces to form dense mats on the river surface, which can trap floating water
hyacinth plants.
